News.title: Burnham must bring obscene £1billion a DAY welfare bill under control or cripple Britain for good
News.content:
Listen to voice of common sense, PM

LORD Jim O’Neill is not some remote economist who lives in an ivory tower.

He was educated at a comprehensive school and got a degree from Sheffield University.



What’s more he is a native Mancunian who has backed Andy Burnham’s devolution plans. So when he talks the PM should listen.

Because the advice is coming from someone who understands his plans for Britain. And it could not be more straightforward.



Don’t bring in a wealth tax. Cut welfare spending. Encourage business enterprise.

On our staggering £3trillion debt Lord O’Neill is crystal clear: “If the country wants to have better longer term growth performances we have got to deal with those things.’’



It is not rocket science.

But the Left-wing Labour backbenchers who sabotaged Sir Keir Starmer’s attempts at welfare reform will fight it in every way possible.

As Mr Burnham puts together his first budget he must remain firmly committed to curbing public sector waste.

After another week of economic gloom in which it was revealed that we spend £1billion a DAY on welfare, he must find ways of bringing this obscene splurge under control.



Any other path would not only lead to the economics of the madhouse.

It would also cripple Britain for good.

The drive to succeed

IF YOU want an example of how Covid chaos is still throttling our economy, then look no further than the ludicrous waiting time for driving tests.

In 2020, learners waited just over a month for a test slot. Six years later it has ballooned to a grotesque 21 WEEKS.

The consequences of this mess are enormous for jobs, growth and the generation of Neets who cannot get work.



Unsurprisingly the delays have had a devastating effect on the number of young people who can actually get a booking and pass their tests.

The proportion of 17 to 20-year-olds holding a full car driving licence in England has almost halved in 30 years.

How the hell will that help almost a million young people get into a workplace where two in three jobs such as plumbing require a driving licence?

Successive governments have done nothing to clear this backlog.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Andy Burnham says he wants to make a difference to people’s lives.



The PM should start by making this crisis a top priority.

News.title: Massive blaze engulfs house and car in London as 70 firefighters scrambled – and locals urged to keep windows shut
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

UP IN FLAMES

UP IN FLAMES Massive blaze engulfs house and car in London as 70 firefighters scrambled – and locals urged to keep windows shut

FIREFIGHTERS are battling a huge house blaze after flames ripped through a two-storey semi-detached home.

Ten fire engines and around 70 firefighters have been scrambled to tackle the inferno – which has also engulfed a car.



Part of the ground floor, first floor and roof are alight at the property on Mount Pleasant Road in New Malden, Greater London.

A car parked in the front garden has also caught alight from the flames.



Station Commander Steve McGhie said the fire was producing smoke which had affected the surrounding area.

He said: “The fire is producing smoke that’s affected the local area, residents nearby are advised to keep their windows and doors closed where possible.

“One of the Brigade’s 32-metre turntable ladders is being deployed as a water tower, allowing crews to tackle the flames from above.”

The Brigade said its 999 Control officers received the first of 24 calls alerting them to the fire at 9.36pm.

Crews were sent from Surbiton, Kingston, Sutton, Wimbledon and surrounding fire stations.

Firefighters remain at the scene as they battle to bring the blaze under control.



The cause of the fire is not known at this stage.

News.title: Super-wealthy Brit asylum hotel boss, 59, wins £76.7m contract to run ANOTHER immigration centre
News.content:
A MEGA-wealthy asylum hotel boss has won a £76.7million contract to run another immigration centre.

Graham King’s Clearsprings Management Limited secured a joint six-year government deal to manage the Haslar Immigration Removal Centre in Gosport, Hants.



King, 59, was raking in around £3.8million a day from the migrant crisis last year, and his net worth stands at £726million.

He first housed migrants in an old cinema where he grew up in Canvey Island, Essex.



His firm now manages accommodation for around 30,000 asylum seekers in sites across the South of England and Wales.

The Haslar site was an immigration removal centre for nearly 30 years until it shut in 2015.

It will house 130 failed asylum seekers and foreign criminals when it reopens in 2027, with plans to accommodate 470 more.

It is next to a golf club and a row of houses, which locals complain they cannot sell.

The Home Office said the procurement process has not concluded, but it held an engagement event for local residents last autumn.

Retired couples like Graham Phillips and Lynne Gould, who live next door to the Haslar centre, cannot sell their four-bed home.



Graham, 75, wants to move because he is worried about foreign crooks living on his doorstep.

He fumed: “People are concerned generally about living in close proximity with 600 people who have no right of residence in the UK and who are waiting to be deported, many of whom have served prison sentences for various crimes.”

News.title: Just 13 Albanian prisoners deported from UK in flop £8million scheme that was meant to send 200 home
News.content:
JUST 13 Albanian prisoners have been sent home in an £8million scheme meant to return 200 of their most serious criminals.

The programme was launched three years ago to make killers, rapists and drug dealers do time in their home country and cut taxpayer costs.



Albanians have been the largest foreign nationality in jails over the past seven years, with their estimated 940 prisoners making up roughly nine to 12 per cent of the non-UK offender population.

A Sun on Sunday probe this year found that five more of their countrymen are jailed every day.



Many are illegal migrants who arrived on small boats.

Others paid up to £20,000 to be smuggled here in lorries.

The UK and Albania announced the jail transfer in 2023, meant to cost £8million over its first two years.

But a source at the Ministry of Justice in Albania said: “The goal was to transfer 200 Albanian prisoners serving more than four years, but only 13 have been transferred so far.”

Among those still awaiting the boot are 15 murderers serving life sentences.

They include Koci Selamaj, 41, who got a minimum of 36 years for murdering teacher Sabina Nessa, 28, in a South East London park in 2021.



He attacked two prison officers at HMP Frankland in County Durham in May 2023.

Housing an inmate in UK prisons costs taxpayers an average of £56,000 a year.

Speaking about the prisoner transfer scheme back in 2023, the then-Lord Chancellor and Tory Justice Secretary, Alex Chalk, said: “This deal will speed up the removal of these offenders and give victims confidence that serious criminals will continue to face justice.”

Albania asked the UK Government to provide £8million to strengthen its prison system to implement the scheme.

The Government agreed to give £4million per year, but has stressed it only pays part of it per prisoner sent back.



The hold-ups are thought to be due to backlogs in Albanian courts, which must recognise a British sentence.

The Government said: “Prisoner Transfer Agreements are only one way we get foreign criminals out of our jails.

“Over 11,700 have been removed since July 2024.”

News.title: Iran-linked hackers ‘shut down UK power plant’ for FOUR days in major cyber attack – after series of hits on US targets
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

REGIME'S STRIKE Iran-linked hackers ‘shut down UK power plant’ for FOUR days in major cyber attack – after series of hits on US targets

IRAN-linked hackers shut down a UK power plant for four days in a terrifying cyber attack, reports say.

The mullah regime is thought to have orchestrated a complete shut-down of the British facility in the most effective attack of its kind.



The alarming cyber assault, reported by The Telegraph, unfolded at the same time as a string of attacks on US infrastructure last month, which affected 12 states.

British officials have not confirmed which power plant was the one affected.



But it is understood the facility was relatively small – and that the attack had no overall impact on Britain’s energy supplies.

It comes after an Iran-linked hacker group breached FBI drones and threatened to target World Cup team buses this summer, according to a report.

Following the UK plant attack, the Government informed the chief executives of power companies, giving advice and direction.

The cyber breach is understood to have been flagged to the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), a public-facing branch of GCHQ.

The centre gives advice to companies on keeping national infrastructure safe from foreign adversaries such as Russia.

It comes amid a spate of warnings on Russian, Chinese, and North Korean hackers from UK and US intelligence agencies.



British critical national infrastructure and government agencies are bombarded by attacks every day, they say.

NHS systems, schools, and commercial manufacturing facilities, including production lines at Jaguar Land Rover, have all been affected.

Chilling hacker groups linked to overseas threats have also stolen customer information from retailers as well as voter records from the Electoral Commission.

Until now, no hacker is thought to have ever successfully brought a British power plant to a total standstill.

The major hack attack in the US sparked floods at dozens of wastewater treatment plants.



Some regional authorities were forced to advise customers to boil their water before consuming it.

On July 26 in Minnesota, the first breach was reported.

It was followed by a string of copycat attacks in Michigan, Georgia, South Dakota and New Jersey.

Government sources told local media the threat was likely to have originated from Tehran.

The UK is massively under-equipped for the scale of cyber threats it faces daily, experts have warned.

News.title: Vigil held for family of four who all tragically died after getting into difficulty in sea off Shoreham
News.content:
A FAMILY of four who were all killed in a devastating sea tragedy have been remembered at a moving vigil.

Hassan El-Khawas, 55, his partner Zeina Alayn, 37, and their daughter Sara, 14, died after getting into trouble in the water at Shoreham, West Sussex.



Their six-year-old daughter Saja was rescued alive and rushed to hospital in a critical condition.

But heartbreakingly, she died three days later on Friday, bringing the family death toll to four.



A vigil was held at Kingston Beach, where the tragedy unfolded, as mourners gathered to remember the family.

A one-minute silence was also held in Shoreham town centre as the community came together in grief.



Reverend Pat Alden told those gathered: “When something happens, whether it’s something we celebrate… or tragic circumstances like this, the community comes together.”

He added: “Shoreham is the sort of place where the community comes together at times like this. We are a very close-knit community.”



The family were British citizens of Palestinian origin who came to the UK from Rashidieh Camp in southern Lebanon, according to the Palestinian embassy.

It is understood they had travelled from their home in north-west London to Shoreham for a day out on Tuesday.

The family entered the water from the beach at Shoreham Fort at around 2pm before getting into difficulty.

Floral tributes have since been left at the beach where the devastating tragedy took place.

Neighbours described the family, who lived in a first-floor two-bedroom council flat, as “warm” and close.



Sara’s school in west London also paid a heartbreaking tribute to the teenager.

The school said: “Sara was a sweet girl, well-liked by staff and students and she will be greatly missed.

“Our thoughts and heartfelt condolences are with her family, friends, and all those affected.



“This news will be deeply upsetting for many students, families and staff.”

Sussex cops believe the deaths were a tragic accident based on CCTV and initial witness accounts.

The force has said there is currently no indication of third-party involvement, although its investigation remains open.

Chief Superintendent James Collis said after Saja’s death: “This heartbreaking update is one we all feared in the aftermath of Tuesday’s tragic events.

“The impact of this tragedy has been felt across the country and I know the Shoreham community, emergency responders and all involved will continue to be affected for a long time to come.”



Prime Minister Andy Burnham described the incident as a “terrible family tragedy”.

Adnan Hmidan, chairman of the Palestinian Forum in Britain, said the community had been left “deeply shocked and saddened”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “The Palestinian, Arab and wider community in Britain, along with the many friends and supporters of our community, have been deeply shocked and saddened by the tragic incident involving the Khawwas family during a day trip off the coast of Sussex.”



The vigil came as a community united to remember a family whose day at the seaside ended in unimaginable tragedy.

News.title: Fury as defence chiefs spend over £120m on military clothing for SAS and Paras from potential enemy CHINA
News.content:
DEFENCE chiefs have spent over £120million on military clothing for the SAS and Paras made by potential enemy China.

The Ministry of Defence has paid out on contracts since 2018, with others agreed since then running until next year.



Among the items supplied are Arctic winter gear for Special Forces, smocks to keep snipers hidden, thermals for air crew and assault balaclavas, we can reveal.

Yet MI5 director general Sir Ken McCallum said last year that threats to the UK from China were “escalating”.



He said: “In the last year we’ve seen a 35 per cent increase in the number of individuals we’re investigating for involvement in state threat activity.

“That means espionage, including against our Parliament, our universities, our critical infrastructure.”



GCHQ, the UK’s intelligence, security and cyber agency, has said China “poses a genuine and increasing cyber risk”.

In May 2024, Anne Keast-Butler, Director of GCHQ, the UK’s intelligence, security and cyber agency, said: “We now devote more resource to China than any other single mission”, and that “China poses a genuine and increasing cyber risk to the UK”.

The companies named in the documents are Cooneen Defence Ltd and Iturri S.A.

The companies supply clothing for the British Armed Forces and the emergency services.



Cooneen Defence Ltd, whose contracts amount to around £75 million, says on its website that garments made for the Ministry of Defence in China “comply fully with rigorous ethical standards”.

But the Clean Clothes Campaign, a pressure group which lobbies for better workers’ rights around the world, claims that up to 84 per cent of all Chinese cotton exports come from the Uyghur region, where up to one million Muslim men and women are being forced to work in labour camps.

Colonel Phil Ingram, a former Army intelligence officer, said it was “utter madness” to buy military gear from a country “that remains a clear threat and a clear and present danger to British values”.

A Ministry of Defence spokesperson said: “We have no direct contracts with Chinese suppliers for combat clothing, and the vast majority of our clothing suppliers are based in the UK.

“Where suppliers source textiles from China, strict rules are in place to protect security and prevent modern slavery.”

News.title: Cut welfare and avoid tax hikes, Burnham is warned by his favourite economist
News.content:
ANDY Burnham’s favourite economist has urged the PM to cut welfare and avoid tax hikes — but turned down a job with him.

Jim O’Neill, a former Goldman Sachs guru, blasted governments for sticking sky-high spending on the credit card.



He told the BBC: “I am a supporter of a more sensible approach to government spending and taxation. As Andy himself has emphasised, genuine welfare reform.

“You are only going to be able to solve those issues and cut the welfare bill if you have a more joined-up approach.”



He said governments had been “scared” to make cuts over the past 15 years — which had left the UK saddled with debt and some of the highest interest rates in Europe.

Lord O’Neill added: “If the country wants to have better longer-term growth performances, we have got to deal with those things.

“I would include the (pensions) triple-lock as well as a more sensible approach to welfare spending.”

The UK is spending nearly £1billion a day on welfare, and has nearly £3trillion of debt after worse than expected borrowing figures.

The gloomy numbers have fuelled fears that Mr Burnham’s Chancellor John Healey will increase taxes in his first Budget in late October in order to fund defence and other spending commitments.

Some in Labour want to see the introduction of a wealth tax — but Lord O’Neill warned this could backfire.



He said: “I’m not a fan of further increases in these kinds of taxes.

“The last thing we should be doing is discouraging genuine risk-taking.”

Lord O’Neill denied falling out with the new PM, insisting he had no policy disagreements with him and is happy to act as an informal adviser.

He said he had turned down a job at No10 because he did not want to have to ditch his other business interests.

Lord O’Neill also suggested Mr Burnham’s upbeat approach to government could get optimistic consumers spending more, boosting the economy.

News.title: Ed Miliband vows bond between Britain and Ukraine 'unbreakable and built to last'
News.content:
Ed Miliband vows bond between Britain and Ukraine 'unbreakable and built to last'

EXCLUSIVE: Speaking as Kyiv marked the 35th anniversary of Ukrainian independence, the Foreign Secretary Ed Milband also praised the solidarity shown by the British people

View 2 Images Ed Miliband said the bond between Britain and Ukraine was 'unbreakable' (Image: Getty Images)

Ed Miliband has vowed the bond between Britain and Ukraine is “unbreakable and built to last”.

‌



Speaking as Kyiv marked the 35th anniversary of Ukrainian independence, the Foreign Secretary also praised the solidarity shown by the British people.

‌



Speaking to this newspaper, Mr Miliband also issued a reminder that Ukrainians were fighting for the security not just of their own country, but for Europe. He said: Mr Miliband said: “Tomorrow, as Ukraine marks the 35th anniversary of its independence, celebrating its sovereignty, identity and culture, the United Kingdom stands proudly alongside the Ukrainian people.

‌



"This day serves as a powerful reminder of the extraordinary strength Ukrainians have shown in defending their country in the face of Russian attack. I pay tribute to their immense and enduring courage.

At least 15 killed and 130 injured in Russian drone strike on Ukrainian shopping mall READ MORE :

Andrew Tate and his brother reported to counter-terror cops after Russia trip READ MORE :

View 2 Images Andy Burnham has vowed to continue to “support Ukraine 100%” after Russia threatened the UK over drone strikes (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

“Ukraine’s defence of its freedom and self-determination matters to us all because of the values they are fighting for and because of what this conflict means for our security in Europe. British people have time and again shown their solidarity with the people of Ukraine during this conflict.

‌



"We will continue to help Ukraine strengthen its security, and work with international partners to ensure Russia faces accountability for its aggression. Our bond is unbreakable and built to last.”

Defence Secretary Wes Streeting will attend a candle-lighting ceremony at the Ukrainian Cathedral of the Holy Family in London to mark the anniversary, where he will pay tribute to Ukraine's resolve, while the PM will co-chair a call of the Coalition of the Willing on Monday.

Earlier this week Andy Burnham warned Vladimir Putin that Britain will continue to “support Ukraine 100%” after Russia threatened the UK over drone strikes.

‌



Mr Streeting said: "Thirty-five years ago, Ukrainians chose independence. Over more than a decade, Putin’s illegal and barbaric war has tried and failed to destroy Ukraine’s freedom and way of life.

“We stand proudly with Ukraine and our support will not waver. They are fighting for freedom everywhere, and we will stand by them until they win.”

It comes as the Ministry of Defence hosts a photographic exhibition and panel discussion at the National Army Museum, showcasing the UK's training effort for Ukraine's Armed Forces through Operation Interflex. Launched in June 2022, it has now trained more than 67,000 Ukrainian defenders.

News.title: Miracle boy defies doctors — years after parents were told he wouldn't survive birth
News.content:
Miracle boy defies doctors — years after parents were told he wouldn't survive birth

Jude Bedingfield, who doctors feared might not survive birth, is now nearing his third birthday after defying expectations while living with three rare genetic conditions

View 4 Images Jude with his mum Heidi, who was warned he may only survive for hours or days (Image: Cover Images)

A little boy is preparing to celebrate his third birthday after doctors warned his parents he might not survive being born.

‌



Jude Bedingfield was diagnosed with three life-limiting conditions while he was still in the womb. Parents Heidi Knight and Ryan Bedingfield were told their baby’s prognosis was poor, and were warned he could survive for only hours or days - if he made it through birth.

‌



The couple had gone into their 22-week scan excited to find out their baby’s gender when doctors instead detected a number of abnormalities. Heidi said: "They told us that they’d found some problems with the baby and took us into a side room, it was such an out-of-body experience. They said he had lots of small different abnormalities which all added up and became a big problem."

‌



View 4 Images The couple recently welcomed a baby girl (Image: Cover Images)

Further tests revealed Jude had three rare genetic conditions - partial trisomy 13, Cri du chat syndrome and Pontocerebellar Hypoplasia (PH) - which come with lifelong disabilities. While doctors could not predict exactly how the combination would affect him, they warned the family he may not survive birth. Heidi and Ryan were also advised several times that termination was an option.

She said: “I’ll never forget one of the consultants sat us down and said it’s as bad as it can get and that our baby was not going to make it. They genuinely thought it was 50/50 if he’d breathe or not.

‌



“All I wanted to do was give him a cuddle. I wanted to meet him alive and have a cuddle, that’s all I thought I was ever going to get.”

Heidi was closely monitored throughout the rest of her pregnancy before Jude was delivered by Caesarean section on September 11, 2023.

Heidi, who is a beauty therapist, explained: “It was such a rush, I’ve never been so terrified in my life. I was about to find out if my baby was going to survive or not. When he was born, he let out this little cry; the only way to describe it is he sounded like a baby kitten. He was then taken away as he needed help breathing.

‌



View 4 Images Minutes after his birth, his parents had the first sign he would survive (Image: Cover Images)

“Before he was born, doctors told us they could use pulmonary surfactant, which can help babies clear their lungs - but we weren’t offered it in there. Ryan suggested it, and after he had it Jude started breathing on his own, and he was able to come over and have skin-to-skin with me, which was the thing I really wanted.

“He wasn’t on oxygen for seven minutes which was the first sign that he was going to be okay.”

‌



Jude was then taken to neonatal intensive care, where his progress quickly began exceeding doctors’ expectations.

Days later, Heidi and Ryan met with his medical and palliative care teams and were told he was doing remarkably well. After 15 days at the Oliver Fisher Intensive Care Unit at the Medway Maritime Hospital in Kent, he was able to go home. Nearly almost three years later, Jude is “thriving” compared with those initial predictions, although he continues to face significant challenges and is not independently mobile.

He is fed through a Mic-Key button in his stomach and has hypotonia, meaning he has low muscle tone and needs support to sit and stand. Heidi describes him as being “like a big baby”. Jude began NHS physiotherapy when he was just a few months old, before his parents decided to also pursue private sessions in the hope of helping his development.

‌



View 4 Images An anonymous £10,000 donation last year allowed Jude to attend his first two-week course of intensive physiotherapy (Image: Cover Images)

The family has since grown, with Heidi and Ryan welcoming seven-month-old daughter Scarlett. Around 18 months ago, they also began fundraising through children’s charity Tree of Hope to pay for intensive physiotherapy.

An anonymous £10,000 donation last year allowed Jude to attend his first two-week course at Ability Therapies in Essex - with his family saying the sessions made a major difference.

‌



Heidi said: “During that two-week intensive course, he learnt to pivot on the floor and change his direction, which seems like such a simple thing, but it’s made a huge difference. It has been absolutely life-changing for him.”

Heidi now hopes Jude’s story can offer hope to other families facing difficult diagnoses after she found support herself through families sharing their experiences online.

She said: “The outcome sounded bleak and we had discussions that no one should have. You think you’re going to have to plan a funeral; it’s horrible. I was adamant that I wasn’t coming home with a baby, and I now have an almost three-year-old - he has exceeded all expectations.

‌



“He is a happy, bright and determined little boy. We totally understand that Jude may be a rarity, but there’s a chance. He’s a happy and determined little boy who loves playing with his toys. We don’t know exactly what the future holds for him, but we want to enable him to live the best life possible.”

The family is continuing to raise money towards physiotherapy and other support Jude may need as he grows.

They are holding a family fun day at The White Horse pub in Sittingbourne, Kent, on Saturday, August 29.
