Andy Burnham has been told that taking Britain back into the EU single market would secure him a general election victory and give him a legacy akin to Tony Blair’s - but would it provide an economic boost the country so dearly needs?

Nick Boles, who served as a minister in David Cameron’s government before quitting the Conservatives in 2019 over the party’s Brexit stance and is now a Labour adviser, has urged the new prime minister to strike a deal with European Union leaders that would protect the continent and boost the UK’s economy.

Mr Boles is calling for the creation of a “European Confederation”, which he says would provide some of the benefits of European integration such as single market access and youth mobility, but without having to accept free movement or being forced to join the Eurozone.

Mr Burnham, whose Makerfield seat voted 64 per cent in favour of leaving the European Union in 2016, has previously said he would like to see the UK rejoin the EU in his lifetime.

According to Mr Boles, the move to access the single market again would also deal a “devastating” blow to the Tories and Reform, securing victory in the next general election and writing Mr Burnham into the history books.

Economically, forging closer ties with Europe could provide a £92bn GDP boost to the UK, according to new economic research.

Commissioned by Best for Britain, which campaigns for full UK-EU reintegration, the research undertaken by Frontier Economics suggests at least 90 per cent of Brexit's economic hit could be recouped by the UK rejoining the EU.

Tom Brufatto, Best for Britain’s executive director of policy and research told The Independent: “While all moves towards closer EU relations are welcome, our polling shows that voters vastly prefer EU membership, especially those prepared to vote for Labour at the next election, and the £92bn GDP boost it would create.

“With the UK being a G7 economy and global military power, full EU membership is the only suitable way for us to benefit from access to the single market while ensuring we have a say over the rules that shape it.”

Polling has shown Britons favour closer ties with the European Union, with research carried out by YouGov in June to mark 10 years since the EU referendum revealing that 59 per cent of voters support a closer UK-Europe relationship, compared with just 20 per cent who do not.

When it comes to the single market, half of Britons support rejoining compared with 26 per cent who do not.

However, Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM, a multinational network of accounting firms, said that rejoining the EU could be a “red herring” when it comes to the economy.

“The impact of rejoining at least partly depends on what that means”, he told The Independent, and he believes rejoining under the previous terms the country had with the EU would have the biggest economic benefit but would be a “harder sell” to the country.

“Let’s say we go back in under the old arrangement. In that case, there would almost certainly be a net economic benefit to the UK. But it wouldn’t offset the losses we’ve already experienced”, he explained.

“If we take the 4 to 6 per cent economic loss from Brexit, that’s largely from a combination of lower/different migration, less investment and trade.

“I don’t imagine we get a renewed surge in inward migration if we rejoin given the UK’s relative underperformance compared to most European countries, and attracting investment would be a struggle given other countries, like Ireland, have created very attractive regimes.

“We would benefit on the trade front, but this is limited given the UK’s small manufacturing sector.”

A Deutsche Bank spokesperson told The Independent that rejoining the single market would primarily benefit the UK in terms of removing economic friction and red tape. 41 per cent of the UK’s exports in 2025 were to EU nations.

“Re-entry would remove the bulk of the friction Brexit created, and crucially it would do so for services — the UK's structural strength”, the spokesperson said.

“Beyond the direct trade channel, single-market membership delivers a productivity dividend that a customs union cannot. Deeper market integration intensifies competition.”

“OBR estimates suggest that the biggest cost from Brexit in the long run can be attributed to a productivity channel - a 4 per cent long-run productivity loss. Re-entry would also restore the labour-supply flexibility, investment certainty and FDI attractiveness that the uncertainty channel of Brexit eroded.”

The UK would have to weigh up what it would have to offer up for entry to the single market, the bank said, disagreeing with some of Mr Boles’s claims.

“The single market's price is sovereignty”, it said. “Membership requires accepting the four freedoms - including freedom of movement - and submitting to EU regulation designed without a UK seat at the table.

“It also implies a budget contribution. These are precisely the red lines that successive governments have ruled out, which is why the single market is the larger economic prize but the smaller political probability.”

Progressive Democrat Abdul El-Sayed became the second Senate candidate to invoke the controversy surrounding President Donald Trump’s relationship with embattled White House aide Natalie Harp — telling her on social media Saturday that her 80-year-old boss “needs his rest.”

The combined shots at Trump and his 35-year-old assistant came as a new report said Harp posted in support of Trump more than 150 times on January 6, 2021, when MAGA loyalists stormed the U.S. Capitol in a bid to keep Congress from certifying his election loss to Joe Biden.

El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate candidate from Michigan, mocked the aging president's stamina after Trump on Friday accused him of having “recently campaigned with a communist fanatic who says that America deserved 9/11,” an apparent reference to progressive influencer Hasan Piker.

“Natalie, I think he's had a little too much iPad for the week. He needs his rest,” El-Sayed quipped.

open image in gallery White House aide Natalie Harp reportedly wrote more than 150 since-deleted social media posts in support of President Donald Trump on January 6, 2021 ( AFP/Getty )

It follows a dig from Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff of Georgia, whose comments thrust Harp, a former far-right cable TV host and 2024 Trump campaign staffer, into the spotlight and sparked heated reactions from the White House.

He alluded to Harp’s relationship with the president during an August 16 re-election campaign rally, and accused Trump of not wanting to “do the job” of president. “He wants to build his ballroom and travel with Natalie,” Ossoff said.

Also Saturday, CNN said it had uncovered scores of posts Harp made on Twitter, now known as X, before her account was apparently suspended.

They included repeated exhortations made January 6 to "FIGHT FOR TRUMP!" according to a screenshot CNN included in its report.

Harp's since-deleted posts also reportedly told Trump, “We love you” and included an altered version of Psalm 43:1 that asked God to vindicate Trump and rescue him “from those who are deceitful and wicked.”

The White House didn't immediately respond to a Saturday afternoon inquiry from The Independent.

open image in gallery Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed poked at Trump after the president accused him of having ‘recently campaigned with a communist fanatic’ ( Reuters )

Ossoff’s crack came after CNN revealed that Harp was among three White House aides who flew with Trump from Turkey to the U.K. on a military jet after he was snuck off Air Force One in response to an Iranian assassination threat.

Unknowing journalists and other members of Trump's administration, including Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, made the trip on the presidential decoy plane.

Democratic strategists were divided over Ossoff's remark, with Anthony Coley, a former Department of Justice spokesperson, telling The Hill, “Timing matters enormously in politics, and Ossoff caught this wave at exactly the right moment.”

Democratic strategist Joel Payne also credited Ossoff with successfully questioning the president's priorities, saying that “if you can make that point with a little bit of hot sauce on top of it, I think that makes for effective politics.”

But David Axelrod, chief strategist for President Barack Obama's winning 2008 and 2012 campaigns, said on social media that the two words Ossoff used to mention Harp “seemed gratuitous and unnecessary.”

“Probably thrilled some in the base, who figured it was just giving Trump a taste of his own nasty medicine. But they distracted and detracted from the power of the message,” Axelrod added.

Harp worked in the White House for more than a year without seeking a security clearance normally obtained by West Wing staffers, MS NOW reported Wednesday, citing two unidentified people familiar with the matter.

It's unclear why Harp didn't apply for the clearance, but she's since filled out the necessary forms at Trump's request after the White House counsel's office and national security officials raised concerns, MS NOW said.

News.title: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions
News.content:
The players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their big-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

News.title: All Blacks stun Springboks in statement win
News.content:
Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry did not begin with the year’s greatest game, but a New Zealand victory against the odds, at high altitude in Johannesburg, has poured intrigue and interest on to a series which was already brimming with them.

The All Blacks’ recent record at Ellis Park, the Springboks’ spiritual home, is by no means shabby – this was their fourth victory from the last six visits – but few fancied Dave Rennie’s galvanised Kiwis on Saturday, against the back-to-back world champions, after a week which had been dominated by chat of officials and law interpretations.

Yet, this stunning victory was almost as comfortable as it was surprising. New Zealand outscored their hosts by five tries to one and, by the end, a 13-player Springboks outfit – both Marco van Staden and Cobus Reinach were sin-binned within a minute of each other – were left chasing shadows in an Ellis Park which had been stupefied into silence.

It was at the beginning of that 13-player period when New Zealand put the game to bed, with Will Jordan crossing for his second try. But the damage had already been done by a cast of Kiwi conquerors. Ardie Savea, captain and No 8, could not have delivered more for the cause; Luke Jacobson and Tupou Vaa’i on the flanks were more than deputies to Savea; the locks, until Josh Lord’s unfortunate departure just before half-time, were magnificent; and, behind them, Cam Roigard continues to look every bit the equal of those phenomenal French scrum-halves. The New Zealand midfield got the upper hand on their much vaunted counterparts, too, on the day of Damian de Allende’s 100th cap for South Africa.

News.title: George Russell king of the sprint and driving with freedom after engagement
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for the sprint race for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix, the first race after F1’s summer break. Kimi Antonelli has had a tremendous first part of the season, leading Lewis Hamilton by 50 points and George Russell by 59 after the first 11 rounds. He has taken six wins to Russell’s two, with Hamilton, Lando Norris and Charles Leclerc all racking up a win apiece.

His start to the second part of the season was not the best, however. A messy sprint qualifying session meant he ended down in fifth, more than 0.2sec behind team-mate Russell, who took a much-needed pole.

Some of the damage was self-inflicted, quite literally. In the first session of sprint qualifying he ran wide at the banked turn 12 and into the gravel. The damage to the floor of his car was attempted to be repaired for the rest of the session but left him lacking downforce. A gap of 0.2sec is not enormous but the other issue was that three other cars – Norris, Leclerc and Piastri – are between him and Russell.

That said, it is not a great worry at this point. The points available in the sprint are relatively small and Antonelli has a healthy margin at this point over his rivals. In any case, there is no guarantee that Russell and Antonelli finish where they will start. Antonelli has shown on numerous occasions that he can bounce back from a difficult session and you have to expect that again here.

The race, which starts at 11am BST, is one-third of the race distance and should be run in dry conditions. There have been persistent showers and a steady breeze at Zandvoort this weekend, but it is not expected to affect the running in the sprint.

Qualifying for tomorrow’s grand prix comes later today at 3pm, which could be a more consequential session.

News.title: Arsenal play like the champions they are as title defence starts with a bang
News.content:
Good evening and welcome to the Emirates Stadium, where the Premier League champions begin the defence of their title. Or, as Mikel Arteta prefers to put it, their “attack” on a new season. A classic Arteta-ism.

The assault starts tonight against Coventry City but our understanding is that Arsenal will be without new £75m midfielder Bruno Guimaraes. We believe the Brazilian has picked up an injury, and it’s not currently clear how severe it might be. Clearly, this is a blow for Arteta. But they should still have enough to get past promoted Coventry… shouldn’t they? We’ll find out soon enough.

Meanwhile, Arteta has said he and his players should relish being Premier League title favourites and the role of the hunted rather than the hunter.

“In the last three seasons, at some point we were first and at some point we were chasing. And you never know what is better,” Arteta said. “But if you give me the choice, I want to be first. I want to be hunted, and I want to be in control of our future, rather than depending on somebody else.”

Arteta called on his players to retain the hunger they had last season.

“We start from scratch, from zero, and we’re going to have to prove we are at the level to go back to that position again,” he said. “We need to show that desire and the ambition to be better than what we were last season, a month ago, a week ago.”

This is Coventry’s first Premier League campaign since they suffered relegation in 2000-01, and they were led to the Championship title by Frank Lampard. They scored the most goals in the Championship and conceded the fewest, and could face one of their former players tonight in Viktor Gyokeres.

Full team news as and when we get it.

News.title: Russell takes Dutch GP sprint pole as Antonelli struggles to fifth
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for sprint qualifying for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix from Zandvoort. This is the last time the race will be on the F1 calendar for the foreseeable future, having been reintroduced in 2021 after a 35-year absence. It will be a shame to see it leave again, but never rule out it coming back, especially with Max Verstappen signing a lengthy contract extension with Red Bull.

What of the competitive action this weekend? As it is a sprint weekend, there is not a lot of preparation time, with just one practice session before sprint qualifying. In that it was a fairly close fight at the top, and it was Kimi Antonelli, the championship leader, who was fastest of all. Behind him was the McLaren of Lando Norris who was 0.121sec adrift then George Russell, who will be looking to kickstart his title campaign here, a further 0.004sec behind him.

Then came the two Ferraris of Lewis Hamilton (0.190sec) and Charles Leclerc (0.289sec) before a fairly significant gap of 0.659sec to Oscar Piastri in sixth. Verstappen was down in 11th, nearly 1.4sec off Antonelli’s ultimate pace but 0.5sec or so ahead of new (and old) team-mate for the weekend, Liam Lawson.

It was a tricky session for the drivers, though, as it began damp on a showery and blustery day by the Dutch seaside. Several drivers ran wide and off the track, though they all avoided anything more serious than gravel rash. The rest of the day looks to be drier but there are still a few showers around and the wind is all over the place, as it often is here.

Sprint qualifying starts at 3.30pm BST and we will be here for all of the updates for the nearly hour-long session.

News.title: Root delivers perfect riposte to captaincy doubters as England hammer Pakistan
News.content:
There was no attempt to be a Ben Stokes tribute act by Joe Root, just a measured captaincy performance very much in his own undemonstrative style.

Root, ever the team man, pushed his bowlers forward to lead England off at the end, recognising the match-winners in a walkover against Pakistan, who were bowled out for 135 in under two sessions.

Victory by an innings and 103 runs inside three days marked a perfect return to the job and put the smile back on England faces for the first time in a long while. The chants of “F--- the ECB” from Trent Bridge, after the New Zealand regime-toppling loss, were replaced by the Yorkshire faithful’s “Roooot”.

There was plenty of scepticism around rebooting the Root captaincy, but he was the only realistic choice. Harry Brook’s batting here was more sensible and at a tempo in the captain’s mould. “He is still learning the art of Test cricket,” Root said. Thrusting Brook into the job would have put more pressure on him, he may well have felt he needed to make risky statements with the bat. Now he can mature under Root and Stephen Fleming.

Tactically, Root was astute and showed enough to suggest he is going to be different this time. The old Root would not have whipped Jofra Archer off after two overs of the Test, but it was a prod that worked as he bowled quicker and more accurately to strike twice with the second-innings new ball, using his new-found skills with a scrambled seam to good effect.

It also showed his bowlers he wanted a fuller length and, from that first hour, they controlled the match and did not let their grip slip.

Root promised to keep the good aspects of Bazball and apply common sense. He continued Stokes’s leg-slip tactic and it paid off with the wicket of opener Azan Awais, and urged Ollie Robinson to bowl with the keeper standing up. England batted at 4.5 an over – a touch quicker than the Bazball years – but it was never reckless, just a calm tempo, with no ramps or scoops.

News.title: Officials selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers
News.content:
Officials in Malawi are selling yellow fever certificates to unvaccinated travellers for around $20 and sending them on their way, a Telegraph investigation has found.



The passport-sized, yellow document, officially called the International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (ICVP), is supposed to provide proof of vaccination against yellow fever, a mosquito-borne virus that kills tens of thousands of people every year.

The jab provides lifelong protection, beginning 10 days after vaccination. Most countries in Africa and Latin America require them for entry, either for all travellers or for those arriving from risk areas.



Yet travellers leaving Malawi through two major airports can get hold of the certificates without ever being vaccinated, according to interviews with multiple travellers and an undercover investigation.



Several passengers who travelled recently from Malawi to destinations including Uganda, Kenya, Ethiopia and China said they had obtained yellow fever vaccination certificates at airports or public hospitals without receiving the vaccine.



One traveller, who recently flew to Uganda for work from Kamuzu International Airport, which serves the capital, Lilongwe, said he was initially told it was too late to get vaccinated because his departure was less than 10 days away.



“When I asked the health officials if I could get vaccinated at the airport, I was told it was too late because I needed to be vaccinated ten days before my trip,” he told The Telegraph.



“But then they offered to arrange the certificate for me for roughly $21,” said the traveller, who asked not to be named. “I had to pay because I could not postpone the trip.”

News.title: Congo gambles on ‘old’ vaccine as new Ebola virus spirals
News.content:
Nearly half of all those infected have gone on to die.

Dr Sania Nishtar, chief executive of the Gavi global vaccine partnership, earlier this week said to beat the outbreak “we must deploy every tool at our disposal”.

She went on: “To avoid this becoming the worst recorded Ebola outbreak in history, it is critical that all effective countermeasure options are brought to bear.

“We have a tool that could help save lives while we wait for [Bundibugyo]-specific vaccines to become available.”

Previous clinical trials have shown that Ervebo is safe, but its effect on other strains is unknown.

The World Health Organisation said in a statement that while it was not known if Ervebo may protect against the Bundibugyo virus, “early laboratory and animal data suggest it may provide some protection”.

Medics told the Telegraph of anecdotal claims that health workers who had been given Ervebo to protect them during an outbreak of the Zaire strain in 2018 to 2020 had not fallen ill during the current Bundibugyo outbreak.

Health workers are at extreme risk of catching the disease because they come into contact with highly-contagious blood, vomit and diarrhoea from dying patients. When they fall sick themselves, they frequently go on to infect their own families.

Giving health workers vaccine jabs to protect them as they tend the sick is a cornerstone of Ebola responses.

The WHO said the vaccine allocation includes 20,000 doses for a Phase 3 clinical trial to understand the impact of the vaccine on the Bundibugyo virus. The remaining 50,000 doses will be used for front-line and health workers as recommended by WHO experts.

Dr Nishtar said: “Having already been licensed for the Zaire strain, we know that Ervebo is proven to be safe.

“And while the signs are that it may not stop transmission – which is essential for ending the outbreak - it could well save precious lives and reduce suffering.”

Health officials warn that the Bundibugyo outbreak centred on DRC’s Ituri province is easily outpacing relief efforts.

The virus is thought to have been spreading for months before an outbreak was finally declared in mid-May and medics have been unable to make up the head start.

An analysis by the Africa Centres for Disease Control meanwhile warned the current outbreak dwarfed all others on record

The current outbreak had almost ten times more cases than any other previous outbreak at a similar stage.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

Sports.title: Leeds hero Anton Stach caps perfect week with goal after launching his own BURGER as own boss calls him ‘weird guy’
Sports.content:
LEEDS’ saviour Anton Stach is a Burger King after he won three points for his team in the same week as launching a new limited edition whopper.

German Stach, 27, netted a late free-kick to see off Nottingham Forest 1-0 at the City Ground but is still “weird” and “crazy” to manager Daniel Farke after his latest venture.



The midfielder made headlines just days earlier after bizarrely announcing that his Moustachi Cheeseburger would be sold at Meat:Stack in the city.

Partnering with the restaurant, Stach is doing it in aid of a children’s charity in Senegal.



And he gave Forest indigestion with a trademark set-piece just two minutes from time on Saturday.

The fan-favourite went down a treat, like his grub, in front of the away supporters.



He signed autographs and posed with a double patty burger for the Newcastle-founded chain on Tuesday before heading to the Midlands for another big victory.

Some of the proceeds from the burger will go towards The Elhadj Diouf Foundation.

And Stach said: “Leeds has felt like home from very early on, and a lot of that is the people and the places around the ground, the businesses fans go to before and after a game.

“Meat:Stack is one of them, and they’ve had a hard time with the building work on their doorstep.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“The Moustachi Burger is a lovely nod to my YouTube channel too.

“This is a team on the rise in a city on the comeback, and support has to go both ways.

“I wanted to back a business Leeds fans care about and raising money for a foundation my family has given so much to at the same time means everything.”

He had stomach for the fight on opening day and lives on a diet of set-pieces according to his boss.

Farke said: “He’s done it time and time again.



“Meanwhile, I trust him in everything. He has even released a burger right now and I never expected him to do this.

“He’s a bit of a weird and crazy guy.

“And because of that, I expected also when he was over the free-kick that he could do something special.



“But again, also this game today was proof that we won’t win anything just with individual quality.

“It was important to show spirit, togetherness, to dig in, to grind out a result, to work for each other.

“And of course, then we have players also who can make the difference and Anton is one of them and we’re happy to have him.”

Sports.title: Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1: Clarke scores 90th-minute winner against old club as Premier League new-boys get opening-day win
Sports.content:
PROMISED LAND Ipswich 2 Sunderland 1: Clarke scores 90th-minute winner against old club as Premier League new-boys get opening-day win

SUPER-SUB Jack Clarke sent Portman Road into bedlam with a deliciously curled winner over Sunderland as the match entered injury-time.

Two years ago, the Tractor Boys lost too many points from winning positions, especially at home, and slipped back down into the Championship with barely a whimper.



Gary O’Neil’s new side are adamant that they won’t be doing that again this season. A rip-roaring game that crackled from the first whistle appeared to be destined for a draw which would have brought uncomfortable memories for those in Suffolk.

After new signing Emersonn had scored a debut goal in the 24th minute to match his £24m transfer fee from Toulouse, visitors Sunderland fought back through a stunning Nilson Angulo free-kick.



That paved the way for Clarke to play the hero from the subs bench, curling the ball into the bottom corner with ice-cool precision in the 90th minute.

Two seasons ago, Ipswich largely stuck to the players who had hauled the club up from League One in successive seasons only to discover that the step up in class was too great for most of them.



This summer, led by new manager O’Neil who has no bond to last season’s team under Kieran McKenna, they have tried another way. The Sunderland way.

Black Cats boss Regis Le Bris brought in 14 new players to his promotion-winning squad and took them into the Europa League places.

So far in this transfer window, Ipswich have signed 12 new players, seven of whom were thrust into the opening day line-up by O’Neil. The returns will not be instant but the points gained from this tight encounter will give them breathing space.

Two of the new signings combined to glorious effect in the 24th minute to send Portman Road wild with delight. Julio Enciso, who was on loan at the club two seasons ago, sped away from two challenges, hurdling his way past Luke O’Nien before picking out Emersonn, who turned the ball over the line.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The 22-year-old Brazilian, signed from French club Toulouse, fell to his knees in a mixture of delight and relief at starting to repay his hefty transfer fee.

He almost returned the favour for Enciso minutes later but the Ecuador international found himself crowded out.

It was another new signing who maintained their lead on the half-hour. Dutch keeper Kjell Scherpen is the tallest player to ever play in the Premier League.

With arms like rotor blades, he had to contort his giant frame inwards to push away a Noah Sadiki header from a free-kick.



For all the excitement swarming around Portman Road whenever an Ipswich player broke a tackle, it was Sunderland who kept opening up the Ipswich defence, with a succession of crosses just evading players in red and white stripes.

The Sunderland players have the advantage of knowing each other’s play. They also have the experience confidence gained from last season’s stellar campaign as they surged into Europe behind the leadership of manager Regis Le Bris and his lieutenant on the pitch, Granit Xhaka.

They began to break up the Ipswich play more frequently and carved out a number of promising attacks.



Ipswich’s luck ran out seven minutes before half-time after new central defender Issa Diop clumsily fouled Xhaka just outside the Ipswich area.

The Switzerland international appeared poised to take the free-kick with his left foot. Instead, it was Nilson Angulo who stepped up from the other side to whip his right-footed shot up and over a static Ipswich wall and in off the underside of the bar.

The equaliser punctured the Suffolk air and brought a reality check to the home fans who remember only too well how many times their side led at Portman Road on their last visit to the Premier League, only to succumb later in the game.

O’Neil clearly had no intention of allowing that to happen, sending his team back out super-charged after the interval super-charged.

The second period began like a basketball game with chances at first one end, then the other. Abdul Fatawu used his trickery to beat defenders at will and sent over a number of enticing crosses, one of which almost converted by Enciso with an imaginative floated effort, before he flicked another Fatawu delivery just wide of the far post.



Daizen Maeda also went close with a glancing header that missed the far post by inches.

It didn’t seem possible that the scoreline would end up at 1-1. Brobbey was usual combative self, muscular as well as determined and it took two Ipswich defenders to charge down his shot following a Reinildo Mandava pass.

It was left to substitute Clarke to send Portman Road into raptures which gave way to unaduterated joy minutes later at the final whistle.

Sports.title: Joe Hart, 39, reveals he’s had hair transplant to give his confidence a ‘boost’ – and shows off results
Sports.content:
FOOTY ace Joe Hart has followed in the footsteps of his pundit pal Wayne Rooney by having a hair transplant.

The former England and Manchester City goalkeeper revealed he underwent a treatment to give his confidence a “boost” – nine months after making his Match of the Day debut.



Hart, 39, acted to save his locks – which he famously showed off during his career in a Head & Shoulders ad campaign – after he realised they were thinning.

The Premier League winner secretly underwent a 2,500 follicle FUE transplant last May.



And he showed off the impressive results while working for the Beeb during this summer’s 2026 World Cup, sparking speculation about his refreshed look.

The keeper’s fresh summer look stunned so many viewers that comedian Paddy McGuiness joked on his football podcast: “Have you seen his hair? An unbelievable transplant. It’s like an Axminster [carpet]. It looks fantastic. I was like, ‘give me the name of that surgeon’.”

Man Utd legend Paul Scholes smiled and added that pundit Hart now “looks like Action Man”.

Since then Hart – who won five league titles with Man City and Celtic, four Premier League Golden Gloves and played for his country 75 times – has opted to come clean about having FUE surgery because, in his own words, “my hair was going.”

And he has also revealed that his hair transplant, ‘has made me feel a lot more easy, comfortable and confident.’

Hart explained the reasons for having FUE surgery in an Instagram post on his hair transplant surgeon’s page.



He said: “I always had really thick hair growing up and loved having thick hair. I felt strong. I felt confident with it. Then my hair started to thin when I was in my early 30s.

“I’ve come away from football now so I’ve got a little bit of time where I can take care of me, and I thought it was the right time to do it.”

Hart’s 2500 follicle procedure was completed byDr Furqan Raja in May last year.

The Leeds-based surgeon has worked wonders with the hair of several leading UK sports and entertainment stars.



He most recently completed new Gladiators star and former England rugby player Joe Marler’s hair transplant to help him retain his trademark Mohawk cut.

About his procedure, Joe said: “When it came to it, I had good people around me and I asked all the important questions of Dr Raja’s team, so I felt comfortable and I felt ready to go. It was always nice and reassuring to know I had the top man doing the work.”

He also revealed that his hair transplant is the reason changing his look. Reflecting on his new buzz cut hairstyle, seen during his World Cup work, Hart said: “I’ve actually changed my style. I didn’t have shorter hair before.

“People have asked me, ‘why have you got it done if you’re only going to have short hair?’ But I like having the option of either. If I want to grow it, I can. If I like it short, I’ll keep it short. Now, I can have the choice.



“Before, if I’d have had short hair, I’d have felt I’d had to have done it because my hair was going.”

Asked by Dr Raja if he’d expected such a transformation, Joe replied: “A good result for me would have been anything that improved what I already had – a little bit thicker through the middle, that I’d see when I was looking in the mirror or getting myself ready. Anything that could have been improved, would have made me feel better.

“And confidence and looks-wise, it has helped me. If it hadn’t have worked it wouldn’t have broken my heart but the fact that it has, has made me feel a lot more easy, a lot more comfortable, confident.”

Dr Furqan Raja explained how he undertook Joe Hart’s FUE hair transplant on his Instagram post.

The surgeon said: “When planning Joe’s procedure, we carefully studied earlier photographs of him to design a natural contour that closely reflected the hairline he previously had.



“Using FUE, we transplanted approximately 2,500 grafts to rebuild Joe’s hairline and add density through his frontal and mid-scalp regions. Then we tapered the area towards Joe’s crown.

“A year on, I’m extremely pleased with how natural Joe’s result looks and there is still further maturation to come.

“It has been fantastic to see the response to Joe’s hair over the past year, and particularly during television coverage of the World Cup last month.

“Seeing Joe and his hair looking so good, as he provided expert analysis on the biggest stage, was particularly satisfying.

“We are delighted for Joe.”



Joe joins a long list of footballers who have had hair transplants.

On the BBC he sits alongside Wayne Rooney who pioneered the procedure in 2011.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Since then, Mohamed Salah, David Silva, Jurgen Klopp, Antonio Conte, Xerdan Shaqiri, Ryan Giggs and Andros Townsend, among other players, have had FUE hair transplants.

Joe joined the MOTD studio panel following his retirement at the end of the 23/24 season and officially became a pundit on BBC’s Match of the Day in August 2024.

Sports.title: Numb Newcastle hero Rob Lee shut himself off from world and wept after tragic death of ‘second dad’ Kevin Keegan
Sports.content:
ROB LEE loved Kevin Keegan and hailed the late Newcastle legend as the “next best thing to my dad.”

And the feeling was mutual as former Toon boss Keegan claimed Lee was his finest-ever signing at St James’ Park.



That is some tribute because King Kev smashed the transfer world record to bring Alan Shearer home from Blackburn for £15million in 1996.

He also brought the likes of David Ginola and Tino Asprilla to the Toon so Lee is in fine company.



So Keegan’s death last month at the age of 75 after a battle with cancer, hit Lee hard.

Former Magpies and England midfielder Lee, 60, was at home on his own when he heard Keegan had passed away.

He emotionally revealed: “I have got to admit I shed quite a few tears that day.

“In fact, I shut myself off from the world for a few hours.

“Within minutes of it breaking, I was inundated with requests for interviews but I had to turn them all down. I was just too numb.”

Lee will be back on Tyneside for the visit of Liverpool, along with many of his former team-mates from the 1990s who together became known — and still are — as ‘The Entertainers.’



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Lee said: “I am quite fortunate because in my capacity as Hornchurch director of football, I’m in Carlisle over the weekend, which is only 50 miles from Newcastle.

“But even if we had been playing in the south west, I would still have been there.

“Nothing in the world would stop me.”

Keegan’s Magpies may have missed out on major honours but Lee regards the five years he played under the legendary England forward were the best years of his life.

Lee, who like Keegan, wore the No 7 black and white shirt, said: “He changed my career and he changed my life.



“People did not believe me when I said I had Keegan posters plastered all over my bedroom walls — but it’s true.

“He was my boyhood hero and I was lucky enough to play under him.

“Believe me, it was the biggest of dreams come true.”

Lee kept in touch with Keegan long after the two left Tyneside and saw him most recently last November.

He said: “It was at a do in Upminster, near where I live. His wife Jean was there with him and my family went along too. It was a great night.



“He was the same Kevin I’d always known. He was witty, bubbly, friendly and oozing charisma.

“And, of course, he stayed long after midnight signing autographs and chatting to people.

“Little could I imagine that would be the last time that I ever saw him in the flesh.”



Lee is now looking forward to a reunion with so many of Newcastle’s greatest-ever players who starred in the Keegan era.

And, of course, the Newcastle versus Liverpool fixture evokes so many memories — some particularly painful.

Lee admitted: “I have lost count of the number of times I’ve been asked if I want to see another 4-3 thriller!

“Let’s not forget we lost the most famous one, which was a result which really cost us.

“There is this myth surrounding Kevin that he’d prefer to lose 4-3 than to win 1-0 — but that’s rubbish.



“Remember, he was a winner throughout his life and winners hate losing.

“Don’t get me wrong, he loved attacking football and he was so proud of that Entertainers’ tag.

“He’d always tell us we had a duty to entertain our public and I think it’s fair to say we managed to do that.

“I cannot recall too many goalless draws when he was in charge.

“I just wish we could have got over the line that season because that’s what Kevin deserved.”



So will Sunday’s afternoon’s Prem clash at St James’ be another high-scoring affair?

Lee said: “Well, I’d love to see it because that would be the ultimate tribute to the man himself — but only with Newcastle winning, of course!”

Since his death, there has been much talk of Keegan being honoured with a statue outside St James’ or even having a stand named after him.



The club have already announced there will be official recognition of the great man.

But Lee feels that perhaps the club should have paid tribute to one of their favourite sons a long time ago.

He added: “Look, it’s all a bit late, isn’t it? Something should have been done years ago.

“I loved Sir Bobby Robson and Alan Shearer is a big mate, but Kevin’s statue should have been erected before anyoneelse’ss.

“Kev rescued Newcastle United from oblivion not once but twice.



“First as a player in the early-Eighties and then as a manager.

“Newcastle were in the old Second Division when he joined as a genuine footballing superstar and led them to promotion.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“And what he did as a manager is now the stuff of folklore.”

There will be tears and cheers for Keegan at around 4.25pm but you suspect that when the minute’s applause is over, no-one will have a bigger lump in his throat than the great man’s greatest-ever signing.

Sports.title: Real Madrid fans fall back in love with ‘GOAT’ Jose Mourinho after action-packed first 15 minutes as Bellingham scores
Sports.content:
IT ONLY took Jose Mourinho 15 minutes to get Real Madrid fans purring once again – but things quickly changed.

The new-old manager got off to a brilliant start in his competitive return on Saturday night, going 1-0 up early against Espanyol.



And The Special One did everything right with an attack-minded XI taking the game to their opponents.

Mourinho, who is back in LaLiga after 13 years away, had an entertaining opening to the season with Jude Bellingham and Arda Guler playing alongside Kylian Mbappe and Vinicius Jr.



Bernardo Silva was deeper in midfield next to Fede Valverde – and Vini even pressed from the front.

Guler, who had an up-and-down time under Xabi Alonso and Alvaro Arbeloa, assisted Bellingham just nine minutes in to leave viewers enthralled.

Madrid passed with purpose, pressing forward and were roaring on the front foot.

Vinicius – a strong target for Arsenal before signing a new contract with Los Blancos, no small part down to Mourinho – showed more energy off the ball than ever.

And England World Cup superstar Bellingham was “playing like 2005 [Frank] Lampard” according to some on social media.

Someone else wrote: “Very promising performance by Mourinho Ball”.

Sports.title: Man Utd chiefs risk resembling Ed Woodward after Hull horror show as knee-jerk buys fail & Carrick endures toughest day
Sports.content:
THE broadcasters did not miss their cue with Manchester United 2-0 down at Hull.

One of the cameras homed in on director of football Jason Wilcox and chief executive Omar Berrada, a duo who have had to adopt deadpan poker faces in directors’ boxes for two years now.



Wilcox and Berrada are entitled to expect much better than the lethargic and leaden performance United served up at the MKM Stadium.

Patrick Dorgu had the benefit of starting all six pre-season friendlies and lasted a half. Harry Maguire and Ayden Heaven partnered each other four times in the friendlies yet looked incompatible.



Many of Michael Carrick’s calls were questionable. Why pick Heaven, United’s rawest defender? Why does he think Dorgu is a winger? Why move Bryan Mbeumo to the wing when he has played all of his pre-season up front? Why put Matheus Cunha up front after a mere 60 minutes there against AC Milan?

Carrick had his worst day as United head coach and a theme has developed. Whenever he makes substantial changes, personnel or tactical, United lose.

The upside is a defensive midfielder is about to beef up United’s soft centre. The downside is the defence will not get overhauled until next year.

With Carlos Baleba expected to be confirmed in the coming days, if not hours, United could feasibly sign a defensive midfielder and a defender in the final days of the window. They will look reactive in a summer that they should have been proactive.

A £70million fee for Baleba was admittedly agreed before the Hull horror show but it should not have taken that long.

Brighton man Baleba knew United wanted him more than a year ago and he spoke with Michael Carrick, as well as future teammates, at the Amex Stadium three months ago.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

Getting Baleba in the building for July would have been doubly advantageous as Cameroon did not qualify for the World Cup. Mbeumo, Baleba’s compatriot, was United’s standout performer in pre-season and the only outfield starter who produced a passable performance at Hull.

United still had two new signings in their side on the opening weekend. The issue is neither is necessarily considered a starting signing when Saturday comes.

Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, on their full debuts, lived up to their squad player billings.

Baleba, a probable long-term partner for Kobbie Mainoo, would be deemed a starting signing. He will not get a kick until next month, at the earliest, due to an ankle injury.

The knee-jerk nature of United’s deal-making has been a theme of their window. Elliot Anderson wanted Manchester City, so it was onto Mateus Fernandes, who took the money and ran to Tottenham. So they turned to Santos.



A deal for Ederson collapsed, so the £35m scheduled to be deposited in Atalanta’s account made its way into Aston Villa’s for Tielemans.

Santos and Tielemans were prudent purchases completed quickly. They should have been good enough to see off Hull, hardly an acid test. Neither passed it.

They will now know how much more demanding it is to pull on the United shirt. Santos has been upgraded from bit-part player at Chelsea to Casemiro’s heir apparent at United. It is an onerous burden on the 22-year-old’s shoulders.



Tielemans recently revealed that his body “switched off” at the World Cup. He was not switched on at Hull and was fortunate to re-emerge for the second half.

A five-year contract for a midfielder who turns 30 next year who made his professional debut aged 16 was excessive. The biggest insult one could level at Wilcox and Berrada is that it was a piece of business reminiscent of Ed Woodward’s days.

Failure to bolster the midfield with an enforcer has contributed to another records-tumbling defeat to Hull – and inflicted reputational damage on Wilcox and Berrada. Finalising incomings in the wake of an August defeat would be another unwanted parallel with Woodward.

It happened last year amid the indecision over which goalkeeper to recruit. While United pondered, Altay Bayindir and Andre Onana chucked the ball in against Arsenal and Grimsby.

A defensive midfielder was always a must at United this summer but they have been complacent at left back and up front.



They have probably left it too late with Lewis Hall and Mikel Arteta has quashed talk of Arsenal cashing in on Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Hall would be the ideal successor to Luke Shaw, into his 13th season at United. Shaw has had three good seasons in 12 and one was in the meaningless and misleading pandemic campaign of 2020-21.

As alarming as United’s defending at Hull was how impotent they were. Striker Benjamin Sesko is back from a long-term shin injury but senior United figures say a new striker is not on their radar.

Joshua Zirkzee, signed on the assumption he was a striker, made one competitive start during Sesko’s three-and-a-half month lay-off and is barely of consideration.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Zirkzee was the first signing of the Berrada and Wilcox era. They’ll need to adopt that poker face again if United are to shift Zirkzee.

Sports.title: Mo Salah ‘to be joined at Trabzonspor by Premier League & Champions League-winning Liverpool pal’ in shock transfer
Sports.content:
MO SALAH is set to be joined at Trabzonspor by ex-Liverpool team-mate Fabinho, according to reports.

Salah, 34, signed for the Turkish outfit in a lucrative two-year £363,000-a-week deal earlier this month.



The Egyptian has been given a hero’s welcome by Trabzonspor fans and he is about to be followed by another big-name signing.

Brazilian midfielder Fabinho, 32, is jetting in for a medical after leaving Al-Ittihad on a free transfer, according to Fabrizio Romano.



The report claims the club has struck a verbal agreement and his agent Jorge Mendes is now looking to wrap up the move.

Should the move be completed, it would reunite Salah and Fabinho after their successful stint together at Liverpool.

The pair spent five years at Anfield and were part of a glittering period that saw them win six trophies.

They won the Premier League, Champions League, FA Cup, Carabao Cup, Uefa Super Cup and Club World Cup during their time together with the Reds.

Fabinho became a fan favourite at Anfield as he played 219 times, scoring 11 times.

He sealed a £40m move to Al-Ittihad in 2023 to play alongside the likes of N’Golo Kante and Karim Benzema.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The Brazil international was part of the team that won the Saudi Pro League in 2025 as well as the King’s Cup.

Fabinho played a total of 111 times for the Saudi outfit but is now looking towards the next chapter of his career.

Salah, meanwhile, will go down as one of the greatest players in Liverpool’s history after ending his incredible nine-year spell at the club in May.

He scored 257 goals in 442 games for the Reds and was crucial in helping the club win two Premier League titles.

But his final season at the club ended on a rocky note as he gave a bombshell interview accusing Liverpool of “throwing him under the bus” over a lack of game time.



He was heavily linked with a move to the Saudi Pro League himself but ended up sealing a shock move to Turkey.

Salah has already made his debut for the club in a 1-1 draw with rivals Kasimpasa.

He played the final 32 minutes of that game before starting a 1-0 Europa League qualifying defeat to Ferencvaros.

Sports.title: Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos show Michael Carrick why Man Utd desperately need Carlos Baleba after stinker vs Hull
Sports.content:
ANDREY SANTOS and Youri Tielemans put the mid in midfield as Manchester United stunk the place out against Hull – and that is being generous.

Michael Carrick‘s new-look pairing were completely ineffective behind Bruno Fernandes and left much to be desired in an embarrassing 2-0 loss.



The opening day competitive debuts for each went terribly as they were hooked after 67 minutes.

In a minor positive, neither Kobbie Mainoo nor Benjamin Sesko had any more luck after coming on, and nobody else had any luck for United.



But with the club still looking to buy a THIRD midfielder of the window, Brighton may well be thinking about bumping up their asking price for Carlos Baleba.

A deal worth around £65million for the player has been agreed but United are so desperate in the centre of the park that they would surely settle for paying even more at this stage.

Historic tough negotiators, Brighton could ask United to throw money at them for Baleba and little argument would surely be put up, he is that big of an addition.

Where Santos and Tielemans were short against Hull, Baleba drives from deep and covers ground for fun.

He is a wide-ranging passer and explosive in marauding across the pitch.

None of those words could be used to describe United’s £85million pair on Humberside.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Santos, who cost £50million of that figure from Chelsea, had been one of the standout performers in pre-season.

He and Mason Mount, another ex-Blue costing £65million, impressed on tour.

But at newly promoted – and massive favourites to go straight back down – Hull, he was stunted.

Brazilian Santos may well have completed 52 of his 56 passes (93 per cent) but almost half of those were safely in his own half.

He lost the ball FIVE times and only produced one progressive carry despite Hull sitting on the edge of their own penalty area.



Usually an adventurous line-breaker, Santos couldn’t impact the game at all.

He committed one foul and ended up making more clearances (three) than chances.

If Santos stumbled then Tielemans fell flat on his face.

The Belgian, a £35million signing from Aston Villa, was even worse.



Another player used to advancing play in possession, he misplaced EIGHT passes and completed less than 50 per cent of his 62 in Hull’s half.

He lost the ball FIVE times trying to get it forward in the middle third and was a hinderance when travelling with it.

Hull nabbed the ball off him on 11 occasions and made light work of getting past him when attacking.

Tielemans made one foul, was dribbled past twice, and made ZERO defensive contributions.



Even Baleba, coming off the back of a tough year on the south coast, will be able to offer more impetus.

And Carrick best hope that it moves along quickly as he seeks to get United going.

Having spoken up the core of the team as something that could push them into a title race, Carrick was left with egg on his face.

Mainoo was left on the bench from the start which frustrated some.



And Santos was described as being “nowhere near good enough at this stage of his career to be a starter” by one fan online.

They added: “Tielemans looked Sunday league level today. I’m honestly speechless at that performance.”

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford sends Man Utd message after dismal Hull City loss
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford sends Man Utd message after dismal Hull City loss

Marcus Rashford made his long-awaited return for Manchester United in their dismal Premier League defeat to Hull City as the former Barcelona loanee came off the bench

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford started the game on the bench (Image: Paul ELLIS / AFP via Getty Images)

Marcus Rashford's Manchester United return came in a dismal defeat to Hull City but the forward believes the team can use it as a building block for the rest of the campaign. England ace Rashford came off the bench against the play-off champions but could not navigate Michael Carrick's side away from defeat.

‌



The Red Devils fell to a 2-0 defeat courtesy of goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy. Rashford was introduced after half-time at the MKM stadium but could not reduce the deficit.

‌



Despite having been widely anticipated to leave Old Trafford after his loan stint with Barcelona, it seems the 28-year-old remains a part of Michael Carrick's plans. The Catalan club decided against triggering the option to sign Rashford permanently, and no other team has swooped in to pay the fee that United require for his services.

‌



Instead, Rashford, who is under contract until 2028, has been awarded the No.9 shirt. The 28-year-old's appearance came more than 18 months after his last competitive outing for the club, against Viktoria Plzen in December 2024.

"After 618 days, I'm back playing with United. I wish the result were better, but it's something we can improve on," Rashford wrote on Instagram after the defeat.

Carrick had nothing but praise for the player he substituted, though. "Pat's fine, we love him to bits. He's a fantastic player, Pat. He's a great character," Carrick said after the match.

Before the Hull fixture, Carrick was questioned about whether Rashford could feature in a central striking role this season. The England international has mainly operated from the left flank in recent campaigns.

Sports.title: Liverpool star told he must tear up his contract to seal return to former club
Sports.content:
Liverpool star told he must tear up his contract to seal return to former club

Celta Vigo want to re-sign Liverpool midfielder Stefan Bajcetic, who has struggled with injuries and has been made available for a permanent transfer by Andoni Iraola

View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic could leave Liverpool (Image: Nikki Dyer/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Liverpool midfielder Stefan Bajcetic has been told he needs to terminate his contract in order to secure a move back to former club Celta Vigo.

‌



Bajcetic has struggled massively with injuries over the past few years and is not part of Andoni Iraola's plans this season. The 21-year-old came through the Celta Vigo academy before joining the Reds in 2020 - and he is now wanted back in Spain.

‌



Having previously been linked with Getafe, it is Vigo who are now reportedly leading the race. Bajcetic made an impact under Jurgen Klopp's management but hasn't featured for the first team in over two years, due to injuries and loan spells.

‌



He has spent time away with Red Bull Salzburg and Las Palmas and Liverpool now want to seal a permanent deal. There is a sticking point, however, with Bajcetic being asked to walk away from his Liverpool contract, which doesn't expire until June 2027.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Spanish newspaper Faro de Vigo report that his former club want him to terminate his deal early - like Mohamed Salah did this summer before joining Trabzonspor - and re-join on a free transfer. They would then put him into their under-21s side initially as a way to nurse him back to full fitness.

Liverpool have just waved goodbye to Curtis Jones, who completed a £30million (€35m) transfer to Inter Milan on Friday. But they are still keen to find a new club for Bajcetic who hasn't delivered on his initial promise.

"If he's happy and we can reach an agreement, it would be a good situation, but I'm not thinking about that right now," Celta Vigo head coach Claudio Giráldez said. "He's a homegrown player; I don't talk about players we don't have.

‌



View 2 Images Stefan Bajcetic hasn't played for Liverpool in two years (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

"If I talk about any of them, it's those who have been here before because we understand that we always have a stronger connection, and on top of that, we have a very good relationship. I coached him. If it happens, great, but I don't talk about players we don't have.”

Offloading unwanted players is part of Liverpool's transfer plan for the remainder of the summer transfer window, which closes on September 1.

‌



"Some deals you have to wait until the end," Iraola explained in an interview with Sky Sports this week. "But the end is the important picture, the one we will have on September 1, because it is true that we are still quite thin."

Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola remains the number one transfer target, but Liverpool have also been chasing Brighton winger Yankuba Minteh. Brighton have rejected a second bid worth £60m for Minteh and want £70m for the former Newcastle player.

Sports.title: Arsenal dealt Kenan Yildiz blow as transfer hopes ended - 'They can offer whatever'
Sports.content:
Arsenal dealt Kenan Yildiz blow as transfer hopes ended - 'They can offer whatever'

Arsenal remain in the market for a new forward but, after missing out on Vinicius Jnr, Juventus have made it clear that they will not sell Kenan Yildiz

View 2 Images Juventus star Kenan Yildiz has continued to impress in Turin (Image: Filippo Alfero - Juventus FC/Juventus FC via Getty Images)

Juventus boss Luciano Spalletti insists Arsenal "can offer whatever they like" but the Italians will not be selling Kenan Yildiz.

‌



The north Londoners failed with an initial enquiry for Yildiz earlier this summer and the Old Lady have now made it clear they're not prepared to entertain the forward's sale.

‌



Juventus are ultimately in no hurry to sell and have the 21-year-old tied down on a contract until 2030, which he signed back in February. Yildiz scored 11 times in 47 outings last term and his displays saw him named the Serie A Rising Star of the Season.

‌



Yildiz has continued to blossom since heading to Juventus as a free agent from the Bayern academy in 2022 and Spalletti is now adamant that, regardless of what figure is produce, the club will not sell their young star.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

He said: “I am perfectly relaxed, because dealing with Yildiz is easy for me. They can offer whatever they like, I want Yildiz here and will always put him on the field. He’s a perfect lad to talk to, he’s mature, and knows he doesn’t need to rush anything.

‌



“His future is already important staying at Juventus, not because there are other clubs who want to spend €100m for him. We are all convinced that we can show the total potential of Kenan, and he is a potential phenomenon of football. The fans are convinced too.”

Arsenal have looked to add another forward this summer despite already bringing in Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge, with the Greek winger impressing in the side's win over Coventry.

View 2 Images Vinicius Jnr opted to remain at Real Madrid despite Arsenal's interest

‌



Vinicius Junior was targeted earlier this summer as his Real Madrid future remains uncertain. Any move would've been the biggest in the Gunners history but the Brazilian instead chose to remain at the Bernabeu, penning a new deal. Since that door was closed Arsenal have been linked with the Juventus star.

Arteta's frontline is already was stocked with the Premier League champions boasting one of the best squads on the planet. Already they are having to leave out individuals who were once regulars. Gabriel Martinelli was a headline omission on Friday night.

Sports.title: Man Utd told new urgent transfer need after awful opening-day defeat to Hull City
Sports.content:
Man Utd told new urgent transfer need after awful opening-day defeat to Hull City

Manchester United have been urged to add attacking reinforcements before the summer ends after they struggled during their shock loss at Hull

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko, Man Utd's only natural striker, was named on the bench for the loss at Hull

Former Manchester United midfielder Owen Hargreaves believes a new striker is needed at Old Trafford because they "didn’t look like scoring" during their loss at Hull.

‌



United were stunned in their Premier League opener by the newly promoted side, and left without even bothering the scoresheet. Benjamin Sesko started the game on the bench, only coming on for the final quarter of the game. Marcus Rashford also appeared as a substitute.

‌



Matheus Cunha began as United's central point in attack but Hargreaves would like to see another No 9 arrive on the red side of Manchester, citing it as an area of concern.

‌



The former player referenced Michael Carrick's biggest successes, which came when they were able to play on the break, but against a Hull side that sat deep and without a genuine No 9 on the pitch, they were stifled in attack.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Hargreaves told TNT Sports: "I think they could probably do with another striker option. I think that showed today, Sesko didn’t start and Cunha played a little bit deeper. He’s a 10, and plays very effective off the left.

‌



"But I do think with (Carlos) Baleba coming into the team, it is a good squad and it is a top four squad, I just think they were at their best last season counter attacking teams. They were at their best counter attacking teams, remember the first ones, Carrick’s first games against City and Arsenal.

"Today where they had possession of the ball they didn’t look like scoring. I think it will be easier when the space opens up. Today there wasn’t that. I think they go back to the drawing board and look at what they can do differently."

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is yet to make an additions to his frontline

‌



United's priority this summer has been bolstering their midfield. Two of their signings, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, began in the defeat at Hull. A deal has been agreed with Brighton and Baleba is poised to become their third midfield addition of the window.

Carrick said on any potential incomings: “I had all eyes on this [game] today, so any other player, at any other club… until he’s ours, it’s not for me to comment on that. If there’s anything to be announced on any player, I’m sure you’ll be the first to know.”

Sports.title: Crystal Palace star stretchered off in tears as injury nightmare returns on opening day
Sports.content:
Crystal Palace star stretchered off in tears as injury nightmare returns on opening day

Crystal Palace's 2-0 defeat at Everton came with a further blow after defender Chadi Riad was stretchered off, having sustained a nasty-looking knee injury

View 2 Images Chadi Riad was stretchered off after being injured (Image: Naomi Baker/Getty Images)

Crystal Palace star Chadi Riad was in tears after sustaining what looked like a serious injury on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.

‌



Riad appeared to twist his left knee while defending a cross from Vitaliy Mykolenko in the second half against Everton. Palace goalkeeper Dean Henderson immediately waved for medical treatment, with the Morocco international in obvious pain and distress.

‌



He pulled his shirt over his head and was in tears as he was stretchered off to warm applause at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Riad was replaced by Takehiro Tomiyasu in the 72nd minute of the 2-0 defeat.

‌



Palace wrote on X: "We're right behind you, Chadi." The 23-year-old's time at the Premier League club has been marred by injuries.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Palace defender Chris Richards told Match of the Day: "You never want to see an injury, Chadi has battled with injuries throughout his career here, my prayers go out to him. We will rally around him, this season is for Chadi."

Manager Pierre Sage added: "At the moment I don't know, I hope it will be better than we think. We await the medical tests."

Chadi joined from Barcelona in June 2024 for a reported £14million fee, yet has only made 16 appearances for the club. Riad was injured in August 2024, with the knee issue keeping him out until December that year.

‌



View 2 Images Chadi Riad appeared to twist his knee (Image: AFP/Getty Images)

Shortly after returning he then sustained a cruciate ligament injury in training and required long-term rehabilitation. Those two injuries kept him sidelined for a combined 430 days.

He returned in the second half of the 2025/26 season and featured enough for the Eagles to make Morocco's 26-man squad for the World Cup. But it now seems that Riad could be set for another prolonged period in the treatment room.

Article continues below

The injury came in a disheartening defeat on Merseyside in Sage's first match in charge as Oliver Glasner's successor. Goals either side of half-time from Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and Thierno Barry earned Everton a 2-0 win.

Sports.title: Arsenal in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez as tensions grow at Atletico Madrid
Sports.content:
Arsenal in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez as tensions grow at Atletico Madrid

Arsenal are still in the running alongside Barcelona to sign Julian Alvarez in the summer transfer window, with the Atletico Madrid striker increasingly unhappy and unsettled

View 2 Images Julian Alvarez is unhappy at Atletico Madrid (Image: Dennis Agyeman/Europa Press via Getty Images)

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta and sporting director Andrea Berta have been in 'frequent contact' with Julian Alvarez and haven't given up hope of signing the unsettled Atletico Madrid striker.

‌



The Gunners are determined to add a world-class forward to their squad before the summer transfer window closes. Alvarez has been focused on leaving Atletico Madrid for Barcelona, but hasn't ruled out a return to the Premier League.

‌



Things have got increasingly messy between Atleti and their star forward - and it could play into Arsenal's hands. Barca saw their €100million (£86m) bid rejected earlier this summer, with Atleti then reporting their La Liga rivals for allegedly tapping up the Argentina international.

‌



Atletico Madrid boss Diego Simeone wants to keep the 26-year-old, but tensions behind the scenes could trigger a transfer. Atleti chief executive Miguel Ángel Gil Marín said on Friday that Alvarez "has not had the best advisors" this summer after saying he wanted to "fulfil his dream" of joining Barca.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Gil Marín's words prompted a not-so-subtle response from Alvarez's agent Fernando Hidalgo, who wrote on social media: "Never ask a liar why he lied. To explain himself, he would have to lie again."

‌



According to ESPN, Barcelona have given up on signing Alvarez, with Atleti refusing to engage in negotiations. They have turned their attention to his Argentina team-mate Lautaro Martinez, of Inter Milan.

AS reports that Alvarez doesn't understand his club's approach to the transfer saga and remains determined to leave before the window closes on September 1. He would still prefer to join Barcelona, but is conscious of not closing the door on Arsenal either.

View 2 Images Arsenal are still interested in a move for Atletico Madrid forward Julian Alvarez (Image: (AP Photo/Manu Fernandez))

‌



Arteta and Berta have been keeping in touch with Alvarez, who is said to appreciate their interest. A move to Arsenal is considered to be 'a welcome emergency solution' for Alvarez, even if he doesn't want to uproot his family from Madrid.

He is continuing to train for Atleti, but is expected to receive a frosty reception from the supporters when they host Villarreal on Sunday. Simeone has tried to cool the situation ahead of what should be his first appearance since the World Cup.

"There's no uncertainty. Miguel Ángel [Gil Marín] spoke clearly," he said. "For me he's a really important player to achieve our objectives. We'll be with him, we'll look after him on the sporting side, because he's our player... He'll be in the squad tomorrow."

Article continues below

"Atlético Madrid, like every big club, is built on great players, and Julián is one of them, as well as being a great professional," Gil Marín told EFE on Friday. "We have to compete with our values, with homegrown players and the best players we can bring in from outside.

"We are going to help Julián and continue to look after him, so he can reach his full potential... We must understand that Julián hasn't had the best advisors around him in recent months."

Sports.title: Bruno Fernandes points the blame after Hull defeat with criticism of Man Utd approach
Sports.content:
Bruno Fernandes points the blame after Hull defeat with criticism of Man Utd approach

Manchester United began their Premier League campaign with a terrible performance and a 2-0 defeat by newly-promoted Hull City on Saturday, much to the annoyance of Bruno Fernandes

View 2 Images Bruno Fernandes was frustrated by the performance against Hull (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Bruno Fernandes said that Manchester United had failed to learn from the mistakes of last season after kicking off the new campaign with a miserable defeat by Hull City.

‌



Hull scored twice from set pieces in the first half and the newly-promoted side comfortably held onto their lead to win 2-0 in Saturday's early fixture. United dominated the possession but barely created anything, with Bryan Mbeumo seeing two efforts comfortably saved.

‌



It was a dreadful way to start the season, with new signings Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos enduring poor debuts. Marcus Rashford was introduced off the bench at half-time, but couldn't make an impact.

‌



United captain Fernandes cut a frustrated figure on the pitch and that spilled over into his post-match media duties. "Same mistakes as we did last season, every away game we give too much of the ball to them," he told TNT Sports. "In the first 20 minutes, the goalkeeper was the one with the most touches.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"We needed to press more, be more aggressive, and then again we need to work on set-plays and not concede these type of goals. Against these types of teams, they are waiting for that moment.

"We knew before the game set-pieces would be a big part of their game. They played all pre-season with a back four but had a five against us for some height, for these moments. The most frustrating thing is that we lost the game."

He added: "We knew [how motivated they would be]. If someone didn't know, it's very surprising. We know in the Premier League these type of grounds are very difficult to play in. You need to match everything in intensity, aggression and everything. We had that apart from two set pieces. That cost us the game.

‌



"I understand the frustration. Every season that starts, we want to compete and go as forward as we can, winning every game. We need them on our side, like last season, believing in us. We know we need more from ourselves too."

View 2 Images Manchester United were woeful (Image: Getty Images)

It was the first game of Carrick's tenure as United's permanent manager and was quite the contrast to the positivity that saw them finish third last season, following his arrival as interim boss in January.

‌



"Some of it was okay, there's bits to improve on. It was never going to be perfect, but going behind and giving ourselves a lot to do makes it more difficult," he said.

"It was a typical one of those games, with a newly-promoted team at home. You can't give them much, they've got a lot to hold on to. After that, we had moments and opportunities but we didn't have the spark to put the chances away or create any more.

"We're bitterly disappointed with the result, but we won't let it knock us. I'm not going into areas [to improve] now, it's for us to know and we'll improve through the week and in the games.

‌



"When we keep getting stronger as a group, that'll come. Today's a game we can't ignore, we have a lot to learn from it - but we will.

"It's one game, the first game of the season. It hurts, of course, but it's one game. It doesn't change the direction the team or the football club is going in. We'll stay calm and in the bubble and focus on next week."
